1. Core Clinical Tension: A 57-year-old agricultural worker presents with chronic atypical chest pain acutely exacerbating over one month with inferolateral ischemic EKG changes, mimicking acute coronary syndrome or myocardial ischemia. However, cardiac imaging unveils an enormous multicystic myocardial mass exerting mechanical compression and regional wall hypokinesia rather than primary atherosclerotic ischemic infarction.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission clinical evaluation concludes following physical examination, baseline laboratory investigations, electrocardiography, chest radiography, and transthoracic echocardiography identifying the large intramyocardial multicystic mass, immediately prior to advanced cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, hydatid serological testing (ELISA), and surgical histopathological examination.
3. Differential Distinctions: Coronary artery disease / acute coronary syndrome is ruled out by negative troponin biomarkers and echocardiographic confirmation that wall motion abnormalities are secondary to extrinsic mass compression. Primary benign or malignant cardiac neoplasms (such as cardiac myxoma, rhabdomyoma, or fibroma) typically present as solid or gelatinous lesions rather than encapsulated, multiseptated cystic masses with daughter cysts and pericystic fibrosis. Congenital pericardial cysts are generally unilocular and extra-myocardial rather than deeply infiltrative multicystic intramyocardial lesions.
case_prompt:
A 57-year-old male farmer presented with a 3-year history of atypical chest pain that had markedly worsened over the preceding month. He reported no weight loss, diaphoresis, fever, rash, gastrointestinal complaints, or respiratory symptoms. His past medical history was notable for ectatic coronary arteries documented on coronary angiography three years prior. He had no known drug allergies and took no regular medications. Family history was non-contributory. He lived in a rural farming community, did not smoke, and denied alcohol or illicit substance use.

On physical examination, he was comfortable and hemodynamically stable. Cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, and skin examinations were completely unremarkable.

Initial laboratory evaluation revealed a normal complete blood count, normal renal function tests, and normal liver function tests. Serial cardiac troponin testing was negative. Electrocardiography (EKG) demonstrated pathologic Q waves in leads III and aVF, negative T waves in leads II, III, aVF, and V6, and left atrial abnormality. A plain chest radiograph was unremarkable except for a prominent aortic knob and enlargement of the left atrium and left atrial appendage with an upturned cardiac apex.

Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal left ventricular size with a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% to 45%, regional hypokinesia in the mid and basal segments of the inferior, inferoseptal, and posterior walls, mild left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, normal right ventricular size and systolic function, mild left atrial enlargement, and mild-to-moderate mitral regurgitation along with mild aortic and pulmonary regurgitation. In addition, echocardiography identified a huge, well-defined intramyocardial multicystic mass involving the posterolateral and basal inferoseptal segments of the left ventricle.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Acute Coronary Syndrome / Ischemic Heart Disease
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Although the patient had a prior history of coronary ectasia and presented with worsening chest pain, pathologic Q waves in III and aVF, and negative T waves in II, III, aVF, and V6, troponin was negative and echocardiography revealed that wall hypokinesia was due to mechanical compression from an intramyocardial mass.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary Cardiac Neoplasm (e.g., Myxoma, Fibroma, or Angiosarcoma)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Primary cardiac tumors typically present as solid intracavitary or infiltrating mural masses rather than encapsulated multicystic fluid collections containing internal daughter vesicles in an agricultural worker.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: a huge, well-defined intramyocardial multicystic mass in the posterolateral and basal inferoseptal segments of left ventricle

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a massive encapsulated intramyocardial cystic left ventricular mass with daughter cysts and pericystic myocardial fibrosis, corroborated by positive echinococcal ELISA serology and surgical extraction of daughter cysts with scolicidal irrigation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Cardiac MR shows a large encapsulated intramyocardial cystic LV mass which is placed intramyocardium of LV diaphragmatic region and involved basal and mid LV inferior, posterolateral and inferoseptal LV segments (measured 107*75 mm) with evidence of pericystic myocardial fibrosis and include multiple different sizes cysts probably daughter cysts

editor_comments: Admission clinical presentation cleanly isolated prior to confirmatory serology (ELISA) and advanced MRI/operative histopathology. All quotes are verbatim.
